name: metis
description: Métis recovers a behaviour model from code, compares it against what somebody said the system should do, and generates human-executable test cases from the part that survives human review. Nothing auto-approves: an unreviewed model produces no tests.

plugins.name: metis
plugins.description: 40 skills for the model-based testing pipeline: analyse a half-formed intent from four directions before it reaches the graph, and refuse the import only when the claim cannot be represented honestly; bring in what a source SAYS the system should do; recover what it ACTUALLY does from a codebase and take that to the approval gate; check the machine is well-formed; walk a reviewer through the gate; generate human-executable test cases and stop at publication; report coverage and what could not be measured; show what a change puts at risk; write the generated specification back where the team reads it; design what to test and how — the techniques a behaviour warrants, the data conditions they need, the level each is asserted at — as a document a person owns and regeneration never overwrites; and run project risk management as a lifecycle across fourteen specialists, computing the arithmetic rather than reciting it, and assess a requirement or a release by declaring what was gathered and what a person must still answer. Skills route through the bundled metis agent, which is generated from the workflow registry.

plugins.name: metis-mcp
plugins.description: The Métis MCP server: 58 read-only tools over the behaviour graph and the knowledge in it — read a model and validate it, coverage and what was unmeasurable, traceability and where the chain breaks, the cases a model would generate, what a diff touches, specifications and requirements, and risk exposure, EMV, PERT, register coherence, and requirement and release assessments that say what was gathered and what is still unanswered. Read-only by default and by construction at that tier (N-8); METIS_MCP_WRITE adds landing and the gates.
